newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices extend gains on Gulf storm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices extend gains on Gulf storm.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices rose another few cents Thursday following news that a tropical depression was swirling around the Gulf of Mexico, sources said.

By late morning, the storm was upgraded to Tropical Storm Danny and posed a potential threat to the Gulf Coast, causing some companies to shut in production and evacuate personnel from Gulf facilities.
Columbia Gas said producers shut in about 90 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) on its system, while ANR said about 140 mmcfd of production was cut due to the storm.
Danny was expected to reach the Mississippi Delta in Louisiana by Friday morning.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices were quoted about four to five cents higher at $2.28-2.29 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub.
Similarly in south Texas prices gained five cents to the low-$2.20s.
In the Permian Basin market, prices rose another six cents to $2.20-2.21, while southern California border prices were up an equal amount to about $2.32.
San Juan prices firmed to about $2.17-2.21, while Waha values edged to about $2.25.
The 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 3 nuclear unit remained off line and may restart Friday, a plant spokesman said. The adjacent unit 2, rated at 1,070 MW, was holding at 70 percent power.
Meanwhile, the 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal plant in New Mexico remained off line for another two weeks of repairs.
In the Midwest, swing prices gained another three cents to about $2.14-2.15. Chicago city-gate prices were also quoted higher in the low-$2.30s.
In the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate were talked mostly in the high-$2.50s to low-$2.60s.
